topic-232-a-fixed-point-approach-for-cau.evolution: Early representatives investigate factorized causes and causal induction. A 2008 method uses local structure to reduce conditional-independence testing when latent causes may exist. Later work studies amortized and hybrid search. PACER in 2026 parameterizes acyclic graphs directly and combines observational and interventional likelihoods, avoiding soft penalties that permit cyclic intermediate structures.
openQuestions: Which interventions most efficiently resolve ambiguity among observationally compatible graphs?
How can discovery methods expose uncertainty caused by hidden confounding or misspecified mechanisms?
topic-232-a-fixed-point-approach-for-cau.overview: Causal discovery seeks a graph of directional relationships from data rather than merely a predictive association. This topic studies conditional-independence tests, latent confounders, structural assumptions, interventional observations, and efficient searches over valid graphs. Identifiability and computational scalability are separate challenges: a fast search cannot recover information the observations do not determine.
topic-232-a-fixed-point-approach-for-cau.title: Causal Structure Discovery from Observations and Interventions
topic-232-a-fixed-point-approach-for-cau.whyItMatters: Learned causal structure can organize hypotheses about a system and guide further experiments, but conclusions depend on assumptions about hidden variables, selection, and mechanisms. Interventions provide additional evidence while introducing questions about their targets, strength, and comparability across experimental settings.

topic-233-multi-source-conformal-inferen.evolution: The substantive conformal representatives include 2019 work on approximate homotopy computation and covariate shift. A 2024 approach uses training-only privileged information to adjust for corruption-induced shift. Recent studies focus on localization and conditional performance; a 2026 backward-conformal method transforms scores to tighten coverage bounds when set size is constrained in advance.
openQuestions: How can localized coverage be improved without unstable estimates in sparse regions?
When is a fixed-size prediction set more useful than a fixed-coverage target?
topic-233-multi-source-conformal-inferen.overview: Conformal prediction converts model scores and calibration data into sets of plausible outcomes. This topic studies efficient computation, conditional or localized coverage, distribution shift, and the trade-off between set size and reliability. Its guarantees concern repeated coverage under stated assumptions, rather than certainty that any particular prediction is correct.
topic-233-multi-source-conformal-inferen.title: Conformal Prediction and Adaptive Coverage Guarantees
topic-233-multi-source-conformal-inferen.whyItMatters: Prediction sets can make uncertainty actionable, but marginal coverage may conceal uneven performance across subgroups or regions. Corruption and covariate shift can also invalidate naive calibration. Useful methods must specify which assumptions support their guarantees and whether tighter sets come at the cost of weaker coverage statements.

topic-234-q-sharp-provably-optimal-distr.evolution: Early work in 1992 studies neural Q-learning with hidden-unit restarts. Conservative Q-learning in 2020 adds a value regularizer to address offline distribution shift. Later representatives investigate distributional estimates and large action spaces; a 2026 critic-centered approach regularizes the action-gradient field to reduce erratic policies while retaining useful curvature.
openQuestions: How can conservatism adapt to the actual coverage of an offline dataset?
Which critic regularizers improve physical action smoothness without obscuring important value differences?
topic-234-q-sharp-provably-optimal-distr.overview: Q-functions estimate the expected return from taking an action and then following a policy. This topic studies how to learn these estimates with neural approximators, how to control overestimation, and how critic structure affects the policy it trains. Offline datasets, large action spaces, and target-update choices introduce different sources of instability.
topic-234-q-sharp-provably-optimal-distr.title: Q-Function Learning, Conservatism, and Critic Stability
topic-234-q-sharp-provably-optimal-distr.whyItMatters: A policy can exploit inaccurate values for actions poorly represented in its data, so accurate fitting on observed transitions is insufficient. Conservative estimates address this risk, while smooth critic geometry matters when value gradients determine continuous actions. These goals can conflict with aggressive value maximization.

topic-235-a-bayesian-framework-for-onlin.evolution: A 1996 analysis examines generalization during online training on finite samples. Later work develops implicit, parameter-free, and strongly adaptive methods. A 2024 classifier benefits from accurate future-example predictions without worsening worst-case regret; a 2026 resource-allocation framework combines online learning with uncertainty bounds for specified social-welfare objectives.
openQuestions: How can learners exploit predictable inputs while detecting deteriorating advice?
Which comparators reflect the practical cost of adapting after repeated changes?
topic-235-a-bayesian-framework-for-onlin.overview: Online learning updates decisions as observations arrive, often without assuming a fixed data distribution. This topic studies regret guarantees, adaptation to easy or changing sequences, abstention, and use of predictions about future inputs. The learner must exploit helpful structure while retaining protection when that structure is absent or misleading.
topic-235-a-bayesian-framework-for-onlin.title: Adaptive Online Learning and Prediction-Assisted Decisions
topic-235-a-bayesian-framework-for-onlin.whyItMatters: Average performance against a fixed comparator may not capture changing needs or uneven consequences. Dynamic guarantees and confidence sequences provide other ways to assess repeated decisions. Computation also matters when each update requires an expensive optimization oracle rather than a simple parameter step.

topic-236-beta-dpo-direct-preference-opt.evolution: A 2009 representative studies randomized pruning for dynamic programs, an earlier computational setting. Parameter-efficient transfer and movement pruning appear in later language-model work. Cross-model Control in 2024 learns a small portable logit adjustment; a 2026 scaling study analyzes how sparsity and repeated training interact when unique data are limited.
openQuestions: Which adaptation effects transfer across model families without degrading their original strengths?
How should sparsity be chosen jointly with data repetition and inference constraints?
topic-236-beta-dpo-direct-preference-opt.overview: Adapting a pretrained language model can involve updating a small parameter subset, pruning computation, or transferring a learned adjustment across models. This topic studies those alternatives alongside model selection and limited-data scaling. Efficiency depends on which parameters and tokens remain active, and on whether adaptation preserves the capabilities needed downstream.
topic-236-beta-dpo-direct-preference-opt.title: Efficient Language-Model Adaptation and Sparsity
topic-236-beta-dpo-direct-preference-opt.whyItMatters: A method that saves trainable parameters may not reduce inference cost, while sparsity can alter both optimization and data reuse. Comparing approaches therefore requires explicit compute, memory, and data budgets. Reusable control mechanisms also need to handle differences in model vocabularies and behavior.

topic-237-active-statistical-inference.evolution: A 1994 ensemble method uses disagreement to select new labels. Later representatives develop pool-based guarantees and information-based selection. Work in 2021 combines uncertainty and diversity for very large batches; a 2026 approach uses foundation-model priors with smaller models to guide acquisition under both class imbalance and noisy annotations.
openQuestions: How can query strategies discover examples that the current model confidently misunderstands?
When should acquisition prioritize minority coverage rather than maximal immediate uncertainty reduction?
topic-237-active-statistical-inference.overview: Active learning chooses which observations should receive expensive labels or measurements. This topic studies uncertainty, diversity, coverage, and statistical inference when the learner controls data acquisition. Batch selection introduces an additional challenge: individually informative examples may be redundant when requested together, especially at large batch sizes.
topic-237-active-statistical-inference.title: Active Learning and Selective Data Acquisition
topic-237-active-statistical-inference.whyItMatters: The value of a query depends on the eventual goal, whether improving a classifier or estimating a statistical quantity. Selection can also amplify existing model biases, so class imbalance, annotation noise, and prior information need explicit treatment. Annotation savings must be measured at comparable predictive or inferential quality.

topic-238-r-3-dao-reactive-recovery-and-.evolution: A 2010 method mines console logs using program analysis and learned event features. Recent work turns repositories into agent environments and evaluates software optimization. SWE-rebench in 2025 continuously extracts interactive tasks to support fresher evaluation; SWE-Compass in 2026 broadens coverage across task types, scenarios, and programming languages.
openQuestions: How can automated evaluations verify intended behavior beyond passing existing tests?
Which benchmarks measure sustained repository work without becoming rapidly contaminated?
topic-238-r-3-dao-reactive-recovery-and-.overview: Software agents must inspect repositories, modify code, run tools, and respond to execution results. This topic studies environments and evaluations that capture those interactions, extending beyond isolated code generation. It also includes statistical debugging and operational analysis, where learning helps identify the causes or locations of software problems.
topic-238-r-3-dao-reactive-recovery-and-.title: Software-Engineering Agents and Workflow Evaluation
topic-238-r-3-dao-reactive-recovery-and-.whyItMatters: Passing a familiar benchmark can overstate capability if tasks are contaminated or cover only a narrow workflow. Realistic evaluation requires executable environments, diverse languages and task types, and evidence that changes solve the intended problem. Automated judges introduce their own reliability questions.

topic-239-a-divide-and-conquer-framework.evolution: A 1998 randomized method clusters pairwise similarities while addressing noisy edges. Later representatives develop spectral and near-linear approximation methods. A 2025 constrained approach uses signed Laplacians and generalized eigenvalues; 2026 work computes lower bounds that certify the quality of practical correlation-clustering and max-cut solutions on individual graphs.
openQuestions: How can clustering objectives reflect application constraints without making solutions opaque?
Which scalable certificates remain informative on sparse, noisy, or overlapping community structure?
topic-239-a-divide-and-conquer-framework.overview: Graph clustering groups nodes using edges that express similarity, disagreement, or constraints. This topic studies spectral methods, hierarchical and overlapping groups, correlation clustering, and scalable approximation algorithms. The graph representation and objective determine what a good partition means, so different formulations can legitimately produce different groupings.
topic-239-a-divide-and-conquer-framework.title: Graph Clustering and Approximation Guarantees
topic-239-a-divide-and-conquer-framework.whyItMatters: Large graphs make exact optimization difficult, but worst-case hardness does not reveal how good a particular heuristic solution is. Instance-specific certificates can narrow that gap. Constraints such as group size or fairness further change the feasible solutions and the computational structure of the problem.
